private.name: OpenAI
private.summary: AI models, enterprise adoption, research and security, including NATO's disclosed large-scale defensive model usage.

latest_development.text: OpenAI said its work with NATO's Communications and Information Agency included up to 300 billion combined input/output tokens per month for authorised cybersecurity work. It gave no contract value, recurring revenue or independently audited defensive outcomes.

private.name: Anthropic
private.summary: Claude AI models, developer APIs, enterprise agents, and a 17 November linked-billing beta that lets eligible enterprise customers pay for their Claude API use inside apps.

latest_development.text: Anthropic's 17 November platform release notes introduced Linked Billing in beta for directly-billed Claude Platform organisations; marketplace-only and subscription-only users are excluded. Inference runs under the app operator's settings and no adoption or revenue was disclosed.

private.name: ByteDance
private.summary: TikTok, Douyin, digital content distribution, AI systems, and proposed private-shareholder liquidity arrangements.

latest_development.text: Reuters on 13 November reported The Information's unverified proposal for a ByteDance repurchase of up to $6 billion of shares at a reported $400 billion private valuation; Bloomberg separately reported a proposed $241.35 per-share price and extension of an IPO-or-liquidity deadline to December 2030. These are attributed press accounts of proposed terms, not a confirmed completed buyback or IPO date.

private.name: Databricks
private.summary: Enterprise data, analytics and AI platforms; announced an approximately $3 billion three-year EMEA expansion and 16 November beta for governed sharing of agent skills.

latest_development.text: Databricks' 16 November product release notes describe beta sharing of Unity Catalog agent skills through OpenSharing and Marketplace. This follows its 11 November planned approximately $3bn EMEA investment and 10 November Netherlands expansion; no new revenue from these developments was reported.

private.name: Stripe
private.summary: Payments infrastructure, bank-embedded merchant acceptance, financial services and software tooling.

latest_development.text: Stripe announced that eligible HSBC UK small-business customers can activate smartphone Tap to Pay in the HSBC Business Banking app. The partnership offers contactless acceptance without an extra card reader but discloses no merchant adoption, contract economics or separate revenue figures.

private.name: Revolut
private.summary: Private financial technology company offering consumer and business banking and payments; Italian branch subject to a preventive court-supervised AML remediation order reported 16 November.

latest_development.text: Reuters, citing a 39-page Milan court ruling, reported that Revolut Bank UAB's Italian operation was put under one-year judicial administration concerning AML controls. Reuters said Revolut itself was not under criminal investigation, services were uninterrupted and oversight applied only in Italy.

private.name: Blue Origin
private.summary: Launch vehicles, engines and space infrastructure.

latest_development.text: Blue Origin reported that its modified BE-4 main oxygen valve passed qualification tests following the May hotfire anomaly; fleet retrofit is underway and investigation closure was anticipated later in November. No new flight date was confirmed.
